# 美股周评 · 2026-09-12：广度跌破一半，风险继续积累

对应周六期次 2026-09-12 · 数据截至 2026-09-11 · 历史回顾补编

正式编号：RI-WR-2026-W37；制作日期：2026-10-02；修订版 v1.1；作者：Sunny。

## 本期判断
本周指数与广度一起回落，综合分数升至 58.2。脆弱性维持高位，金融压力仍低。风险主要来自股票内部结构走弱，配置继续保持谨慎。

## 本周市场

| 观测指标 | 上一期 | 本期 | 变化 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 综合分数 | 52.48 | 58.18 | +5.70 分 |
| 市场宽度 | 54.40% | 49.79% | -4.61 个百分点 |
| 金融压力 | 34.10 | 32.95 | -1.15 分 |
| 市场脆弱性 | 91.32 | 91.78 | +0.46 分 |
| 市场风险 | 46.24 | 59.37 | +13.13 分 |
| 参与度风险 | 38.25 | 48.62 | +10.37 分 |

周频模型：Level 4，参考风险仓位 50%；信号日期 2026-09-11。综合状态与广度截至 2026-09-11。[1]

截至 9 月 11 日，SPY 较前周下跌 0.77%。有效样本中位于 200 日均线上方的股票占比降至 49.79%，一周减少 4.61 个百分点。与上一期相比，本周的变化更直接：指数下跌的同时，参与上涨的基础也在收缩。[1][2]

综合分数由 52.5 升至 58.2，仍在谨慎区间。市场风险升至 59.4，参与度风险升至 48.6，脆弱性为 91.8；金融压力仅 32.9。风险正在向参与结构扩散，但尚未表现为普遍的融资压力。[1]

## 通胀约束下，等待反弹扩散

8 月 CPI 环比上涨 0.4%、同比上涨 3.4%，核心 CPI 环比上涨 0.3%、同比上涨 2.4%。总体通胀仍高，能源价格上行增加了政策判断的难度。9 月 FOMC 即将召开，宽松预期需要接受新数据检验。[3]

模型风险等级为 Level 4，参考风险仓位降至 50%。在广度收缩、脆弱性高位的组合下，暂时没有提高整体风险敞口的理由。后续即使指数反弹，也需要观察上涨是否扩散到更多股票；若参与面没有改善，反弹的基础仍然偏窄。

## 继续关注

| 方向 | 观察内容 |
| --- | --- |
| 市场广度 | 观察广度能否重新扩张，参与度风险能否停止上升。 |
| 风险敞口 | 维持 Level 4 模型参考，关注高脆弱性是否持续。 |
| 9 月 FOMC | 核对利率决定、声明措辞和经济预测，重点看通胀约束。 |

## 数据口径

观察区间：2026-09-04 至 2026-09-11。模型指标采用当期存档版本，SPY 价格采用 2026-10-02 提取的冻结记录。[1][2]

广度为有效美股样本中价格高于 200 日均线的占比，样本覆盖范围可变；不是标普 500 专属广度。历史分母未完整保存。

SPY 周度变动按复权收盘价计算，未另行重建分红再投资；文中价格变动不是策略回报。[2]

综合状态按原始分数划分：<35 建设性，35-<50 中性，50-<65 谨慎，65-<80 防御，≥80 压力。低频组件与周频风险信号可能滞后；模型分数不表示危机概率。

本稿为历史回顾，编制于 2026-10-02。v1.1 修改文字，保留原数据版本；截图与后来重算的序列可能存在差异。

## 资料限制

本稿以美股内部结构为主，SPY 用作指数价格代理。未进行事件因果分析，也未纳入截止日之后公布的数据。

存档质量检查通过，源时效标签为 current。信号日期见正文；通过质量检查不代表数据均已更新。

## 披露

本材料由 Residual Inertia | 余势制作，仅用于研究与信息交流，不构成投资或证券交易建议。模型输出不代表实际账户仓位。作者实际持仓及利益冲突信息未在本报告中披露。

- [2] [Massive 价格数据方法：本稿使用冻结的 SPY 价格记录](https://massive.com/docs/rest/stocks/aggregates/custom-bars)
- [3] [BLS：8 月 CPI，9 月 11 日发布](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/cpi_09112026.htm)

## This week in markets

| Measure | Previous | Current | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Composite score | 52.48 | 58.18 | +5.70 points |
| Market breadth | 54.40% | 49.79% | -4.61 pp |
| Financial stress | 34.10 | 32.95 | -1.15 points |
| Fragility | 91.32 | 91.78 | +0.46 points |
| Market risk | 46.24 | 59.37 | +13.13 points |
| Participation risk | 38.25 | 48.62 | +10.37 points |

Weekly model: Level 4, 50% reference risk exposure; signal date 2026-09-11. Composite and breadth observations end 2026-09-11.[1]

As of September 11, SPY fell 0.77% from the prior week. The share of eligible stocks above their 200-day averages fell to 49.79%, a weekly decline of 4.61 percentage points. Compared with the previous issue, the change was more direct: the index declined while the foundation of participation contracted.[1][2]

The composite score rose from 52.5 to 58.2, remaining in Caution. Market risk increased to 59.4, participation risk to 48.6, and fragility reached 91.8; financial stress was only 32.9. Risk is spreading through participation structure without yet appearing as widespread financing stress.[1]

## Inflation constrains policy; a rebound needs broader participation

August CPI increased 0.4% month over month and 3.4% year over year. Core CPI rose 0.3% month over month and 2.4% year over year. Headline inflation remained elevated, and higher energy prices complicated the policy assessment. With the September FOMC approaching, expectations of easing must be tested against new data.[3]

The risk model was Level 4 and reference risk exposure declined to 50%. Contracting breadth combined with elevated fragility provides no present basis for increasing overall risk exposure. Even if the index rebounds, watch whether gains spread to more stocks. Without improving participation, the rebound would still rest on a narrow foundation.

## What to watch

| Area | Observation |
| --- | --- |
| Market breadth | Watch whether breadth expands again and participation risk stops rising. |
| Risk exposure | Retain the Level 4 model reference and monitor persistent high fragility. |
| September FOMC | Check the rate decision, statement language and economic projections, with particular attention to the inflation constraint. |

## Data and methodology

Observation window: 2026-09-04 to 2026-09-11. Model readings use the archived vintage for that period. SPY prices use records frozen on October 2, 2026.[1][2]

Breadth is the proportion of eligible U.S. equities trading above their 200-day moving averages. Coverage varies; this is not S&P 500-only breadth. Historical denominators were not fully preserved.

Weekly SPY price changes use adjusted closes. Dividend reinvestment was not independently reconstructed; these changes are not strategy returns.[2]

Composite states use the unrounded score: below 35 Constructive; 35 to below 50 Neutral; 50 to below 65 Caution; 65 to below 80 Defensive; 80 or above Stress. Lower-frequency components and weekly signals can lag. Scores are not crisis probabilities.

This is a retrospective prepared on October 2, 2026, not a publication made during the historical week. Version 1.1 revised commentary while retaining the original data vintage. Screenshots and subsequently recalculated histories may differ.

## Limitations

This report focuses on internal U.S. equity-market structure and uses SPY as an index price proxy. It does not perform event-level causal analysis or incorporate releases after the observation cutoff.

Archived quality checks passed; the source freshness label was current. Signal dates are stated separately. Passing quality checks does not mean that all inputs have been updated.

## Disclosure

Prepared by Residual Inertia | 余势 for research and information only. This is not investment or securities-trading advice. Model outputs do not represent actual account holdings. The report does not disclose the author's holdings or conflicts of interest.
